name: Shellwork — Shelf Accumulative Sculpture Collective
description: Shellwork is a Shelf-based art movement centered on accumulative sculpture — massive, growing installations built from salvaged industrial waste, broken cyberware, discarded packaging, and found objects layered over months or years onto fixed anchor points throughout Tier 1 districts. Pieces are never finished and never signed — anyone can add, and the collective considers authorship a Tier 3 concept. The movement's most famous installation, 'The Grandmother' in Block 6 South, has been growing since 2211 and now stands fourteen meters tall, incorporating an estimated 40,000 individual objects. Shellwork artists are called Adders, and the highest internal status goes to those who contribute pieces with the best stories — not the best aesthetics.
cultural_impact: Shellwork installations have become informal landmarks and navigation points throughout the Shelf, functioning as community bulletin boards, memorial sites, and meeting places — their removal by city maintenance crews is treated as a violent act and has sparked three riots since 2215.
locations: The Bone Yard, Tier 1 Industrial Fringe
story_hooks: A Tier 4 gallery wants to 'preserve' The Grandmother by buying the land, encasing it in climate-controlled glass, and charging admission — the Shellwork community must decide whether preservation or destruction is the worse fate.

An Adder discovers that a piece added to a Shellwork installation six months ago contains a functioning surveillance node — and the installation has been watching a resistance organizer's home ever since.

A demolition order has been issued for Block 6 South under corporate development rights �� the community has 72 hours to respond, and the Shellwork collective is not unified on whether to fight or to document and relocate.
